description: Use it when the user wants a site's logo, colors, fonts or brand guidelines, or to design, build or animate anything for a product whose site is known. Reads a website in a headless browser, the way it is drawn, and saves its brand in one folder: the logo files cut from their real background (PNG and SVG), the colors with where each one is used, the fonts, the first screen, a brand card, and the app store icon and screenshots when the site links to its apps. BRAND.md is the file to read first and card.png the picture to show the user; brand.json is for tools and _brand.yml for Quarto and Shiny. With facts, it also saves what the site claims about itself, each claim with its page, in FACTS.md, for copy that needs the site's numbers, customers, quotes or prices; a launch film does not read it. An App Store or Google Play listing works as the address, a social profile is refused, and a deeper page is read from the home page. For font files and their licenses, use make_font_kit instead. The brand playbook (makersmcp_playbook) has the whole job. (easybrandkit 0.4.2, on this machine.)

facts.description: Also save what the site claims about itself, each claim quoted with its page: numbers, testimonials, customers, prices, integrations and security standards, read from the home page and, where its robots.txt allows, the pricing, customers, security, integrations and about pages it links to. For copy that needs those claims. Takes longer (default false).

out_dir.description: Folder to save into, absolute or relative to /tmp/churn-hnvpfmca. Default: easybrandkit-<host>, where <host> is the site's host without www or the port. A run replaces what an earlier run of this tool left there once it has ended well, and one that fails or is canceled leaves it as it was: give each version its own out_dir. The folder must be empty or hold an earlier run of this tool: any other folder stops it.

stores.description: Also save the icon and screenshots of the App Store and Google Play apps the site links to, and the profile pictures of its X, YouTube, LinkedIn, Threads and Pinterest pages (default true). Set to false to skip them.

timeout_seconds.description: Give up after this many seconds (default 120, or 240 with facts). A slow site, or a kit made from a loading screen, can need 240.

url.description: The product's website, like https://linear.app, or its App Store or Google Play listing. A deeper page is read from the home page, and a social profile is refused.

wait_seconds.description: How long to wait for the result, counted from the start of the call, before returning a job_id to wait on. Some clients end a call after 60 or 240 seconds; 45 is safe in all of them.

name: make_brand_kit

continued.description: True when this call continued the job an identical call started, instead of starting another.

docs.description: The notes the text shows, and where each one is.

expires_at.description: When the download links stop working.

url.description: Where to download the file, when the job ran on a server.

folder.description: Where the kit saved its files.

last_line.description: What the kit was doing last.

next.description: What to do next, as the Next line says.

passed.description: For checks: whether the check passed.
